_note: Sanitized reference, real workflow. Any credential display names replaced with placeholders. Node logic, classification prompt, and status-transition rules are unchanged.

trigger.name: Outbound Platform Event
trigger.note: Fires on any outbound-platform event (open, click, reply, bounce) for a lead created by file 2.

stages.name: Set IDs
stages.note: Extracts lead_id, campaign_id, event_type, to_email, from_email from the webhook body.

stages.name: Wait -> Get Lead Data -> Get Message History
stages.note: Pulls the lead's custom fields (including the CRM contact ID stashed by file 2) and its full message thread.

stages.name: If Replied? -> Classify Reply (LLM) / skip
stages.note: Only a genuine REPLY event triggers the classification call - opens/clicks/bounces skip straight to the CRM-update step with no LLM call at all, since there's no reply text to classify. The prompt is intentionally narrow: exactly one of INTERESTED / NOT INTERESTED / OUT OF OFFICE, nothing else.

stages.name: Set CRM ID, Sequence Step, Status
stages.note: Status-transition rule: NOT INTERESTED marks the CRM record COMPLETED immediately; a reply landing on the sequence's final step without an INTERESTED verdict also marks COMPLETED (the sequence ran its course without a positive signal); anything else stays IN PROGRESS. This is the idempotency-relevant part - a redelivered webhook for an already-COMPLETED lead just re-writes the same terminal state, not a flip-flop.

stages.name: Wait -> Update CRM Contact
stages.note: PATCHes the CRM contact with the sequence step, event type, status, and both raw email addresses from the event - so a human looking at the CRM record sees the full outbound-side context without needing to open the outbound platform at all.

why_this_exists: The outbound -> CRM direction. Closes the loop without a human having to notice a reply and manually update the CRM - the whole point of a bidirectional sync is that neither side requires a person to keep them consistent.
